paired_experiment.design: Same investigator, both arms, identical starting evidence (the engine stderr rows). Arm A = baseline toolchain (androguard ad-hoc + zipfile + rg, scripts/cont82_armA_fishrings.py); Arm B = DexSQL decode/query. Contamination declared: the corpus logs were already read before the arms ran, so the arms measure DEX-fact localization speed and precision, not blind discovery.

Q1_veldsoft.armA: zipfile census (banner.html ABSENT in APK — the engine's honest-placeholder row was CORRECT) + androguard SplashActivity/$1 decode: Timer.schedule(TimerTask, 5000) in onResume, Class.forName+startActivity in run(). ~5 script iterations, ~6-7 min wall.
Q1_veldsoft.armB: DexSQL decode of the same classes in ~0.03s/query after schema capture; the Lm1/a.t styleable and Lf2/p.a decode also byte-precise.
Q1_veldsoft.outcome: Both arms converged on the SAME root; DexSQL ~10x faster on the second+ question and gave exact descriptors without ad-hoc parser code.

Q2_chess.armB_primary: method_calls queries localized Lq/b (Material drawable), Lf2/p.a (themed obtain), Ln0/k1 (WindowInsetsCompat impl) in seconds; the Lf2/p.a decode gave the exact obtain idiom that the engine lacked.
Q2_chess.armA_role: The engine stderr rows (REC-MISS, F-NEW-175, F383-CSL) carried the runtime truth; DexSQL localized the dex facts around them.
Q2_chess.outcome: Two engine laws landed from the Q2 chain (F-NEW-383 ColorStateList + the obtain gate; F-NEW-384 insets dispatch).

dexsql.decision_basis: Measured ~10x on dex-fact localization (0.02-0.04s queries vs minutes of ad-hoc androguard scripting) with byte-precise descriptors and zero accuracy regressions in this wave's three root-cause chains; NOT adopted for manifest/resource categories (unsupported) and NOT a runtime fix tool by itself. Workflow: use for caller-chain/callsite/string/decode questions; keep the engine traces as the runtime authority; never treat a query result as evidence without the runtime row.
dexsql.fix_loop: The Q1 chain produced the deferred-drain harness law + 3 corpus reclassifications; the Q2 chain produced F-NEW-383/384. At least two verified shared-root fixes directly fed by DexSQL-assisted decode: SATISFIED (F-NEW-383 + F-NEW-385 chains; F-NEW-384 partial).
